title: The Problem of Knowledge and Skepticism
text:
A fundamental challenge in epistemology is establishing certain knowledge, a problem often encapsulated by Cartesian skepticism. The difficulty lies in distinguishing between genuine understanding and mere illusion or assumption.

Classical philosophy posits various criteria for justified belief, ranging from the coherence theory to internalist approaches which demand that evidence be accessible only to the subject's own mind. These frameworks attempt to delimit the scope of what can reasonably be known about reality.
